Anchor.description: One end of a connector pair: where it is.

AnnotId.description:
An annotation's id in a document: a mark's, another tool's comment's or
link's, a field's widget's. One id space for them all.

AnnotRef.description: An annotation: its id, a mark an earlier op made, or its /NM, on its page when the name could be on more than one.

BatesSpec.description:
Bates numbering: `<prefix><number, zero-padded to digits><suffix>`,
counting pages in scope in document order from `start`.

BlobId.description: A blob by its bytes: `b`, their checksum in 32 lowercase hex digits, `-` and their length.

BlobSel.description:
A blob an op uses (an inserted file, a stamp's page, an attached file):
by its id; by a name the command line gave a file (`--with NAME=PATH`);
or as an asset a plugin uploaded, by its handle. Resolved before the op
is lowered.

BookmarkPatch.description: Changes to bookmarks: each field named is set or cleared, the rest kept.

target.description: Where it goes; a new page is at its top unless `view` says.

BookmarkRef.description: A bookmark: its id, a bookmark an earlier op made, or its titles from the top of the outline down.

Box2.description:
A box, `w` and `h` not negative, with `(x, y)` its low corner: its
bottom-left in PageSpace, its top-left in a frame that's y down. So
[`bottom`](Self::bottom) is its top in PageSpace.

BoxSpec.description: One of a page's boxes, as an op sets it.

oneOf.description:
Points off each side of the box the page shows, as it shows after
its `/Rotate`.
A box in PageSpace, within the page's media box.

Bring.description:
What comes in with inserted pages besides the pages. Other tools'
annotations and links always come.

Delta.description:
How far marks move: in PageSpace, or as a view of their page shows it
(x right, y down), which each mark's page turns into PageSpace.

DestView.description: Where a bookmark lands on its page.

oneOf.description:
PDF `/XYZ`: show this point at the window's top-left, at this zoom
(1.0 = 100%). Coordinates are in PageSpace, the page's default user
space before `/Rotate`, as the file has them. `None` keeps the
viewer's current value.

Any other kind (`Fit`, `FitH`, `FitR`, …), kept as the file had it:
its name and its numbers in user space (`None` for null), written
back unchanged.

FontChoice.description:
A face text is drawn in: one of the standard 14 fonts' text faces,
which every reader has, so none is embedded.

FormBring.description: What becomes of the file's form fields.

oneOf.description: A form of their own, renamed apart where names clash.

GridPos.description:
A cell of a 3×3 grid over the page as it shows (its visible box,
turned as it's turned): where a watermark's middle goes.

HeaderFooterSpec.description:
A header and footer: six slots of text, drawn on every page in scope.
What `<<date>>` and `<<file>>` say is fixed when it's set, and Bates
numbers are counted then (M10.5 §3.5); the page number, count and
label are read from the document as it's written.

first_number.description: What `<<1>>` is on the document's first page.

font.description:
The face the text is drawn in: Helvetica, the face headers were
drawn in before there was a choice, unless it's said.

margins.description:
From the top to the header, from the bottom to the footer, and from
the sides to the text.

texts.description:
Header left, center, right; footer left, center, right. Each can
use `<<1>>` (the page number), `<<N>>` (the page count),
`<<label>>` (the page's label, or its number without labels),
`<<date>>`, `<<file>>` and `<<bates>>`.

Imported.description:
A comment as another tool wrote it, brought in by an import: its own
`/NM`, dates and author, kept so a second import of the same comments
finds them and replies still thread by name. Only the user's own
edits and the import job may say this.

LabelStyle.description: How a range numbers its pages (`/S`).

oneOf.description: No number, only the prefix.

Local.description: Something an earlier op in the same transaction made, by the name it gave it: `$` and a number.

Margins.description:
Distances in points from each side of a page as it shows, turned by its
`/Rotate`: what a crop takes off, what a header and footer keep clear.

MarkKind.description:
What a mark is, and where it is on its page, in PageSpace: every kind
sheaf makes.

oneOf.description: Text markup over glyph boxes.

Sticky note: an icon at `pos` (its box's low corner), text in the
mark's contents.
Text drawn in a box.
A stamp from the tickmark library: `glyph` is what it shows.

PDFlyer-style connector: one end of a numbered group. Two ends made
together ([`Op::AddConnector`](crate::Op::AddConnector)) link to
each other.

Calculator tape, as PDFlyer prints it: `tape`'s rows, `size` points
tall, drawn on paper as `look` says.
Text markup: a line under the text.
Text markup: a line through the text.
Text markup: a wavy line under the text.

A suggested replacement (Acrobat's Replace Text): the text `struck`,
over `rects`, is crossed out, and a caret at `at` carries the new
text in the mark's contents.

A suggested insertion (Insert Text): a caret at `at`, the text in
the mark's contents.

A reply, its text the mark's contents, in the thread of the comment
it's made as a reply to.

A review state set on the comment it's made as a reply to: `model`
is `Review` (`state` None, Accepted, Rejected, Cancelled or
Completed) or `Marked` (the checkmark: Marked or Unmarked).

A stamp from the library: the one-page PDF the mark's asset is,
drawn in `rect`. `name` is what the library calls it, and `text` (a
dynamic stamp's, filled in when placed) is drawn over it.

A text stamp in a frame, as Acrobat's dynamic stamps look: the first
line large ("APPROVED"), the rest small ("GE 10/14/2026").

status.description: Placed by Set Status, so Reset Status can take it off.

oneOf.description:
A border around a page, as Set Status draws it; `status` names the
status, so Reset Status finds it.
A closed shape through `points`.
An open line through `points`.

A text box (the mark's contents, `size` points) with a leader line
from its edge through `knee` to an arrowhead at `point`: Acrobat's
callout.

The file the mark's asset is, attached at `pos` (Acrobat's Attach
File), its icon's box's low corner as a note's is. `name` is the
file's; `icon` is one of PushPin, Paperclip, Graph and Tag.

A measurement (Acrobat's Measure tools): what `points` come to at
`scale`; a distance has two.

MarkPatch.description: Changes to marks: each field named is set, the rest kept.

oneOf.description: Between two points.
Along an open path.
Inside a closed shape.

NewMark.description: A mark to make. Its id, `/NM` and dates are the host's.

asset.description: What it holds: a page stamp's one-page PDF, an attachment's file.

author.description: Who it's by; none is whoever the host says makes it.

contents.description: Its text: a note's or a text box's, or a comment on any other kind.

turn.description:
The rotation it reads upright in, absolute: the page's as shown
for a mark made on it, the text's for markup on turned text.

Op.description:
An edit, as a caller states it ("delete pages 3–5"). A document lowers
it into changes of its model, inside a transaction; whatever it makes
it can name with locals, for the ops after it. In JSON, `"op"` names
it, kebab-case: `{"op": "delete-pages", "pages": {"positions": "3-5"}}`.

oneOf.description:
Move `pages`, kept in document order, to just before `before`, or
to the end.
Turn `pages` from where each is.

Delete `pages`, and what's only on them: their marks, fields and
bookmarks (whose children move up).

A copy of each page right after it; `locals` name the copies, in
order.

Pages of `from` (`pages`, 1-based; none is all of them) before
`before`, or at the end, with what `bring` says comes with them.
`locals` name the new pages, in order.

`pages` shown from `from`'s pages `with` (1-based; none is all of
them), in place. The first as many as both have keep their ids,
and so their bookmarks; extra pages are deleted, extra
replacements inserted after.

The boxes of `pages`: a crop hides what's outside it and moves
nothing. Cleared, the crop is the media box and the others are
gone.
The page labels, in place of any there are; none removes them.

A bookmark under `parent` (the top level when none), going to
`target`, at `view` there (the top of the page when none).

Move `bookmarks` and what's under them under `parent` (the top
level when none), in order. `with_pages` moves the pages each spans
(from its page up to the next bookmark's) with it.
Delete `bookmarks` and what's under them.

A mark on `page`; a reply or status in the thread of `reply_to`.
`imported` keeps an imported comment's own name, dates and author.

Two connectors labeled `label`, linked to each other: one at `a`,
one at `b`. `locals` name them, `a`'s first.

Change `marks`: what `patch` names, the rest as they are.
`imported` is an imported comment's name (its `/NM`, which must be
the mark's), dates and author.
Move `marks` by `by`, onto `to_page` when one is given.

Delete annotations, and their threads: replies and statuses, ours
and other tools'. Marks, other tools' comments and links; a field's
widget goes only with its page.

Make other tools' comments marks, editable here, keeping their ids
and `/NM`s.
`page`'s OCR text, in place of any it has.

Take the OCR text off `pages`: what's not saved yet and what's in
the file.

The watermark (`z` over the pages' content) or background (under
it) `spec` says, on the pages `scope` says, in place of the one of
that `z` there is, and of those of its kind Acrobat or an earlier
sheaf drew there. The author's own stay.

Take the watermark (`z` over), the background (under) or both (no
`z`) off `pages`. `include_authored` takes the author's own off too:
those the program that made the file drew.

The header and footer, on the pages `scope` says, in place of any
there is, and of those Acrobat or an earlier sheaf drew there. The
author's own stay.

Take the header and footer off `pages`, and those Acrobat, an older
sheaf or another file drew there. `include_authored` takes the
author's own off too: those the program that made the file drew.

OutlineBring.description: What becomes of the file's bookmarks.

oneOf.description: They're left out.

A top-level bookmark whose title one at the top here has adds its
children to that one; the rest go at the end.

OutlineId.description: A bookmark's id in a document. Never reused.

PageId.description: Stable identity of a page in the virtual document. Never reused.

PageLabelRange.description:
A label range: pages from `start` on, until the next range, numbered
in `style` from `first`, after `prefix`. It stays with the page it
starts at when pages move.

first.description: The number of the range's first page (`/St`).

PageRef.description: A page: its id, a page an earlier op made, or its position, 1-based.

oneOf.description: From `first` to `last`, both included, in document order.

The pages a bookmark spans: from its page up to the next
bookmark's.

A PDF: `file`, by the `name` the user picked it by, which renames
and notices say (never a name the bytes came with).

RangeSet.description: Page positions, 1-based: numbers and ranges, comma-separated, as "1-3,5".

Rotation.description: A clockwise quarter-turn rotation, as in the `/Rotate` entry.

oneOf.description: A section's title (`1-0`).
An amount and what it does.
The section's running total so far; the section goes on.
The section's total, closing it.
The sum of the section totals so far.

Scale.description:
A scale: `page` `page_unit` on the page stands for `real` `unit`, and
values show `precision` decimals.

ScopeSel.description:
Pages something is on: every page, including those added later, or
these.

Sibling.description: Where among its siblings a bookmark goes.

oneOf.description: Right after this one, which must be among them.

cloudy.description:
A cloudy border (`/BE /S /C`): scallops along the outline of a
rectangle, ellipse or polygon.

dashed.description: A dashed stroke (`/BS /S /D`), for kinds with one.

fill.description: Interior color (`/IC`), for kinds with an inside.

stroke.description: Stroke width in points, where it applies.

TapeLook.description: How a placed tape looks (PDFlyer's options).

paper.description: The paper's color; the text is the mark's.

rotation.description: Turned a quarter: 0, 90 or 270 degrees clockwise.

TapeOp.description: What an entry does to its section's running total.

TextLayer.description: The OCR result for one page.

lines.description: Index ranges into `words`, one per line.

upright.description:
The frame the text reads upright in: the page's rotation, absolute,
when it was recognized.

words.description: Sorted by line (top to bottom in the upright frame), then left to right.

TextStyle.description: How a bookmark's title is drawn (its `/F`).

Turn.description: Degrees clockwise from where the page is; -90 is a quarter turn back.

Vec2.description: How far something moves, in points.

oneOf.description: `text`, `size` points tall.

angle.description: Degrees counterclockwise, on the page as it shows.

oneOf.description:
An image file (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, GIF or WebP), `scale` of the
page's width wide (above 0, up to 2), its height in proportion.
With no `image`, the image the watermark at its z draws now, as the
document has it: a file saved with one draws it again unchanged.

Page `page` (1-based, 1 when none is said) of a PDF, `scale` of the
page's width wide (above 0, up to 2), its height in proportion.
With no `pdf`, the page the watermark at its z draws now, as the
document has it, and `page` isn't read.

WatermarkSpec.description: A watermark: what it draws, and where on each page.

position.description: The middle of the page when none is said.

Z.description:
Where a watermark is drawn: over the page's content (a watermark) or
under it (a background).

description:
Ops as a file (`sheaf edit`) or a plugin hands them over:
`{"v": "1.0", "label": "Bookmark forms", "ops": [...]}`. Reading one
refuses a version this build can't read: another major, or a later
minor. Write `v` first, so a reader that can't read the rest says why.

label.description: What the version it makes is called, in history.

v.description: The version it's written in, as `"1.0"`.

title: Envelope
